title: From two fingers to a full hand.
lead: Each step has a clear goal, so progress is easy to measure. Some steps overlap, and publishing everything openly runs the whole way through.

phases.title: Phase 0: Foundation
phases.summary: Set up the project and get the hand model moving in simulation.
items: Project structure, public repo and licenses
Checked the Fusion 360 export and wrote down its problems
Converter from the CAD export to a MuJoCo simulation model
Simulation viewer with a slider for every joint
Simulated motions checked against the real hand

phases.title: Phase 1: Thumb and index, moving smoothly
phases.summary: Make the 8-joint prototype move cleanly on stepper motors, controlled from the computer.
items: Firmware with smooth speed-up and slow-down for all 8 motors (tested on the computer)
Motors switch off when idle to stay within the power supply
Python control library that works on the simulation and the real hand
Digital twin software: move a slider on screen and the real joint follows (not yet tried on the hand)
Still to do: first power-on, motor direction checks and calibration of each joint
Still to do: basic motions like open, close, pinch and point

phases.title: Phase 2: Smart servos
phases.summary: Swap the steppers for Feetech SCS0009 servos that report their own position.
items: One shared data cable for all servos, through an FE-URT-1 adapter
Same Python code as before, with a new motor driver underneath
Read back position, load and temperature
Digital twin shows the measured joint positions, live
Compare steppers and servos for speed, precision, force and noise

phases.title: Phase 3: Mechanics and a realistic simulation
phases.summary: Make the hardware robust and the simulation behave like the real thing.
items: Study tendon routing, friction and tension, and model the tendons in simulation
Soft TPU fingertip pads
Measure real speed, friction and play, and tune the simulation to match
Redesign the thumb toward five motions, like a human thumb
Weigh the printed parts and update the model

phases.title: Phase 4: Full hand
items: Middle, ring and little fingers, based on the index design
Decide where the motors live: palm or forearm
Electronics and power for the whole hand on the servo bus
Full-hand simulation model with around 20 or more joints

phases.title: Phase 5: Sensing
phases.summary: Give the hand a sense of touch and a camera.
items: Touch and force sensing in the fingertips
A camera to see the hand and what it holds
Sensor data in the Python library and the simulation

phases.title: Phase 6: AI control
phases.summary: Teach the hand to move by itself.
items: Control the hand by moving your own hand in front of a webcam
Learn from recorded demonstrations
Train in simulation on cloud GPUs, then transfer to the real hand
Optional: larger-scale training in NVIDIA Isaac Sim or Isaac Lab

phases.title: Phase 7: Seeing and grasping
phases.summary: Use the camera to find objects and handle them.
items: Detect objects with the camera and plan how to grasp them
Harder tasks: turning objects in the hand, using tools, everyday objects
Publish benchmarks and results
